text: Instructions for a coding agent: divide the repository by asking what the system would lose without each part, write short true notes, record relations with evidence, write tours whose steps are connected. Installed with codeatlas skill install.

Every command prints JSON so a coding agent can parse it. scan, build and serve are for people; outline, context, agenda, path, validate and apply are the agent's whole interface to the semantic layer — it never edits .codemap/ directly.

A pure function from (path, text) to facts — symbols, imports, references — so its output can be cached by content hash. Python and JS/TS have hand-written walkers; Go, Java, Rust, C, C++ and C# share one spec-driven walker that also infers local and field types, so svc.place() can name its class; any other tree-sitter grammar gets a generic pass, and docs and config get outlines.

Builds the static site the viewer reads. Before any agent has run it drafts regions from the directory tree; the nested layout lets every file reserve the box its symbols need, so zooming in never makes boxes overlap. Output is split into graph.json, a search index fetched on first use, and chunks capped at a few thousand symbols.

pyproject.toml, CI on three operating systems, a release workflow that publishes to PyPI with trusted publishing, and the Pages workflow that builds this very map from the .codemap/ committed in this repository.

Turns names into edges with a ladder from most to least certain — self/this, same file, imports, star imports, same package, a name unique in the repository — and records how each edge was found. A name that matches nothing is dropped rather than guessed. Per-language import rules live in resolve_langs.py; a SCIP index, when given, replaces the heuristic references of the files it covers.

The part agents write — regions, assignment rules, notes, relations and tours — stored as text in .codemap/ so it is reviewed like code. It changes only through validated changesets, and every note, relation and tour step records the hash of the code it describes; the next scan compares hashes to flag what went stale.

A rebuildable SQLite cache under .codemap/cache/: files, symbols, edges, the parse cache and rename aliases. graphdata.py loads it and derives what layout, agenda and the site all need: file-to-file weights, PageRank importance and in-degrees.

Lists files through git (or a directory walk), classifies them linguist-style so vendored, generated and binary files stay off the map, and re-parses only files whose content changed, in worker processes. Files whose size and mtime are unchanged are not even opened. Resolution then runs over the whole repository, so an incremental scan gives exactly the index a full scan would.

One small but realistic fixture repository per language, plus end-to-end checks from scan to site data: incremental equals full, renames keep their notes, changed code makes notes stale, tours must be connected, boxes never overlap.

A React and deck.gl app that only reads static JSON, so the map can be hosted anywhere. Semantic zoom switches between regions, file dots and symbol boxes by their on-screen size; chunks load as files open; tours play along the scanned call chain. Its build is written into src/code_atlas/web and shipped inside the Python wheel.
